name: Amraphel
overview: Amraphel is a male figure identified in Scripture as the King of Shinar, a region mentioned in Genesis 14:1. Beyond his royal title, the biblical record provides no additional tribal affiliation or personal notes about him. His role is primarily defined by his kingship in the early post-Flood narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Amraphel' appears as a proper name without a given meaning in the biblical text. He is also titled 'King of Shinar,' indicating his rule over the ancient land of Shinar, but no specific linguistic meaning is provided for this title in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships or connections for Amraphel beyond his designation as King of Shinar. There are no listed relatives or tribal affiliations associated with him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Amraphel's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his role as a regional monarch during the time of the patriarchs, specifically noted as King of Shinar in Genesis 14:1. His mention situates him among the early post-Flood rulers and contributes to the historical context of the Genesis account.
